To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PLS and PCR models, developed to predict TBF of tablets prepared from SPRESS® B830, were different in terms of predictability.
the predictability of PLS models for lubricant sensitivity assessment of SPRESS® 820 tablets was significantly different from the predictability of PCR models.
the predictability of multivariable models, calculated with benchtop NIRS, assessing lubrication impact on the TBF of SPRESS® 820 is dependent on the lubrication fraction and the multivariate method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of NIR calibration model for prediction of TBF of tablets prepared with lubricated SPRESS®, a model drug.
the development and evaluation of NIRS calibration models to assess the lubricant sensitivity of SPRESS® tablets.
the assessment of the impact of lubricant fraction and blending time on tablet breaking force of SPRESS® 820.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PLS comprehensive model has better predictability than the individual 0.5% and 1% w/w models and the 0.25% w/w model has better predict ability than the 1% w/ w model.
PLS regression models are more predictable than PCR models, and comprehensive PLS models are more predictable for the prediction of TBF of lubricated SPRES® B820 tablets.
the predictability of NIRS-based models is dependent on lubrication concentration and multivariate methodology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the predictability of multivariable calibration models, calculated using offline near-infrared spectrometry, assessing impact of magnesium stearete fraction, blending time and compression force on tablet breaking force of SPRESS®B820, was statistically compared.
PLS regression models are superior to PCR models and PLS comprehensive (with 0.25%-0.5% w/w MgST) is superior to individual (0.25%,0.5%, or 1% w/w) MgSt PLS regression models.
the PLS calibration model was able to predict the TBF values with a high degree of precision and accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the selection of the lubricant fraction should be carefully considered during the development of the NIR models, as the fraction of the lubricant has a significant impact on model performance.
the predictability of calibration model is affected by the lubricant concentration and adopted multivariate regression method.
the predictability of multivariant models, which were calculated by NIRS for lubricant sensitivity assessment of tablets, may depend on lubricant fraction and adopted multivariant methodology.
